steps.objective: Declare a path parameter with a specific Python type to enable automatic parsing and validation.

What happens when an invalid value like 'foo' is passed for an int path parameter?

steps.objective: Create a custom Enum subclass inheriting from str to define predefined valid values for a path parameter.

steps.objective: Use a custom Enum type annotation for a path parameter to restrict input to predefined model names.

steps.objective: Write a FastAPI endpoint that accepts optional query parameters with default values and returns different responses based on whether the parameter is provided.
requirements: How do you declare an optional query parameter with a default value of None in a FastAPI function?
What happens to the response when the optional query parameter is not provided versus when it is provided?

steps.objective: Create a FastAPI endpoint that accepts a boolean query parameter and uses its converted value to modify the returned data.
requirements: How do you declare a query parameter of type bool in a FastAPI function?
Does FastAPI automatically convert string 'true'/'false' from the URL to Python True/False for bool types?

steps.objective: Define a Pydantic model class inheriting from BaseModel with required and optional fields, then use it as a parameter in a POST endpoint.
requirements: How do you import BaseModel from pydantic?

steps.objective: Write a single FastAPI endpoint that simultaneously accepts path parameters, query parameters, and a request body defined by a Pydantic model.
requirements: How does FastAPI distinguish between path/query parameters and request body parameters in the same function?
Can you mix standard types (like str) for query parameters with a Pydantic model for the request body in one endpoint?

steps.objective: Declare a Pydantic model attribute using `Field` to add extra information that appears in the generated JSON Schema.
requirements: How do you import and use `Field` from pydantic?
What is the correct syntax for passing `json_schema_extra` inside a `Field` declaration?

steps.objective: Define a Pydantic model where an attribute is a list containing submodels (e.g., a list of nested objects).
requirements: How do you declare a list of Pydantic models as a single attribute type?

steps.objective: Create separate input and output Pydantic models for an endpoint that accepts plaintext data but returns sanitized data.
requirements: How do you define two different Pydantic models to handle input validation and response filtering?
How do you annotate a FastAPI endpoint function to accept one model and return another?

steps.objective: Raise an HTTPException with a specific status code and custom headers to handle errors.
requirements: How do you import and raise an HTTPException in FastAPI?
How can you add custom headers to an HTTPException response?

steps.objective: Create a dependency function that returns data required by a path operation.
requirements: How do you declare a dependency using the Depends() utility?
What is the correct syntax for defining a callable dependency function?

requirements: How do you declare a dependency using a Python class instead of a function?

m1-s1.title: Write a Python function that imports FastAPI and creates an instance of the FastAPI class.
m1-s1.summary: Import FastAPI and create an app instance to start building your API.
you_will_learn: Assign it to a variable named app

blocks.heading: Initialize Your FastAPI App
blocks.body: To start building your API, you must first import the `FastAPI` class from the `fastapi` module. Then, create an instance of this class and assign it to a variable named `app`. This `app` object is the main point of interaction for defining your routes.

items.title: Import Syntax
items.text: Use `from fastapi import FastAPI` to bring the class into your current scope.

items.title: Instantiation
items.text: Call `FastAPI()` with parentheses and assign the result to `app`.

blocks.title: Basic App Setup

blocks.text: Do not forget the parentheses `()` when calling `FastAPI()`. This creates the instance; omitting them leaves you with just the class definition.

docs.label: `fastapi dev` with path or with `--entrypoint` CLI option

m1-s2.title: Write a Python function that defines a path operation decorator for a GET request at the root path.
m1-s2.summary: Use @app.get('/') to define a GET path operation at the root.
you_will_learn: Define a function for the root path

blocks.heading: Defining a Root GET Path Operation
blocks.body: To handle requests to the root path '/', use the @app.get('/') decorator. The string 'get' inside the parentheses specifies the HTTP method. Place this decorator directly above your function definition.

items.title: The Decorator Syntax
items.text: Use '@app.get("/")' to tell FastAPI that the following function handles requests for path '/'.

items.title: Specifying the Method
items.text: The second argument inside the parentheses, like 'get', defines the HTTP operation (method).

blocks.title: Root GET Endpoint

blocks.text: You can use other methods like @app.post() or @app.delete() for different HTTP verbs.

m1-s3.title: Write a Python function that defines a path operation decorator for a POST request at a specific path.
m1-s3.summary: Learn to use @app.post('/') to handle POST requests at a specific path.
you_will_learn: Define a function for the operation

blocks.heading: Defining a POST Path Operation
blocks.body: To handle POST requests, use the `@app.post()` decorator. Place it above your function and specify the path in parentheses, like `/items`. This tells FastAPI to call your function when a request arrives at that URL using the POST method.

items.title: The Decorator Syntax
items.text: Use `@app.post("/path")` directly above your function definition.

items.title: HTTP Method Name
items.text: The string inside the decorator, such as `post`, defines the HTTP method.

blocks.title: POST Request Example

blocks.text: The decorator syntax `@app.method()` is a Python decorator that modifies the function below it to register it with FastAPI.
